title: Packing documents into sequences
goal:
Appendix B says GPT-3 trains on sequences of the full $n_{\text{ctx}} = 2048$ tokens, "packing multiple documents into a single sequence", with an end-of-text token between documents and no special attention mask. Write three functions on integer token lists:

- `pack_documents(docs, n_ctx, eot)` appends `eot` after every document, joins them into one stream, cuts the stream into consecutive pieces of `n_ctx` tokens, and drops a final piece that is shorter than `n_ctx`. It returns an integer array of shape `(n_sequences, n_ctx)`. The paper doesn't describe the boundary cases, so these are this exercise's choices.
- `document_ids(seq, eot)` returns an integer array that labels each position with the index of its document within the sequence. An `eot` token belongs to the document it ends, so the label changes on the position after it.
- `cross_document_pairs(seq, eot)` counts the pairs $(i, j)$ with $j \le i$ where the query position $i$ and the key position $j$ lie in different documents. A causal mask with no document mask lets the model attend to all of them.
hints: Build one flat list first: for each document, extend it with the document tokens, then `eot`. Slice that list at a multiple of `n_ctx`.
`np.cumsum(seq == eot)` counts end-of-text tokens up to and including each position. Shift it right by one to count only the earlier ones.
For each query $i$, the keys $j \le i$ in a different document are those with `ids[j] != ids[i]`.
Return `np.zeros((0, n_ctx), dtype=int)` when no full sequence fits.
